headline: Choppy but recovering: Monday Sep 14 actually closed DOWN 1.49% at 167,970.66 (-2,541pts) as fresh Mideast escalation — Houthi strikes on Saudi energy facilities, reported US-Iran naval exchanges, a Saudi pipeline shutdown — pushed oil toward $100+; that's worse than the ~-0.62% snapshot logged in yesterday's review, another case of an intra-session read understating the real close. Today (Tue Sep 15) buying returned hard: KSE-100 closed UP 0.85% at 169,392.32 (+1,421.67pts) on broad-based strength in autos/cement/banks/E&P/OMCs/power, helped by SBP's FX reserves hitting an all-time high $21.4bn after a $3bn Eurobond raise. But the geopolitical backdrop is genuinely worse than the 'Hormuz talks progressing' framing of the past couple of reviews — this is now real, repeated military exchanges (Houthi attacks Sep 8 and again Sep 15, Saudi's pipeline shutdown Sep 13), not just diplomacy, with Brent near $107 and oil up >8% this month. Drawdown from the Jan ATH is still ~10.6% — unchanged range, not deepening toward 15%. Portfolio ~Rs 10.07M, P/L ~-Rs 185,300 (~-1.81% on cost) — a bit better than yesterday's ~-1.99%. No holding moved more than ~3% since yesterday. AVN's EXIT call and the AICF/MICF dry-powder redeployment both remain unexecuted (holdings unchanged in index.html).
market: KSE-100: Monday Sep 14 closed at 167,970.66, DOWN 2,541.20pts (-1.49%) — day range 167,441.63 to 170,437.73 — as escalating Middle East tensions and oil-supply concerns triggered broad selling that intensified after 2pm. This confirms yesterday's review logged an early snapshot (~169,453, -0.62%) that undersold the actual decline — the third time in recent reviews an intra-session read has diverged meaningfully from the real close; treat any 'as of ~14:30 PKT' figure in this file as provisional until the next day's review confirms it. Today, Tuesday Sep 15: buying returned from the open (+1.19% by 9:35am) and held into the close, KSE-100 finishing at 169,392.32, UP 1,421.67pts (+0.85%) — day range 169,189.29 to 169,988.11, volume 372.01M shares, 280 gainers vs 166 decliners. Two threads drove it: (1) POSITIVE — SBP's FX reserves hit an all-time high of $21.4bn after Pakistan raised $3bn via a dual-tranche Eurobond, a genuine structural improvement in external-financing risk; (2) NEGATIVE but not enough to offset today — the regional security situation has materially escalated versus how the last two reviews framed it. This is no longer just 'Oman-mediated Hormuz talks' — Houthi militants attacked Saudi energy facilities in Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran on Sep 8 (70+ wounded), reports emerged of a second undisclosed US-Iran naval exchange, Saudi Arabia shut a critical pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz on Sep 13, and fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia were reported again today (Sep 15). Oil is up >8% this month, Brent ~$107/bbl, WTI ~$102.68/bbl. This is real, repeated military action, not diplomacy-in-progress — the single biggest macro risk overhanging PSX right now, and worth tracking daily rather than assuming the last review's 'talks continuing' framing still holds. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) is ~10.6% (169,392.32 close) — essentially unchanged from recent reviews, still past the 10% dry-powder trigger but not deepening toward the 15% heavier-redeployment threshold. AVN: no new company news beyond the already-known Sep 2 H1 FY26 loss filing; still down heavily, EXIT call unexecuted across many consecutive reviews. EFERT: no new Q3 results or fresh dividend announcement; the Sep 3 payment (Aug 10 ex-date) remains the last confirmed one. Pharma/DRAP: a new nuance — the Federal Minister for Economic Affairs has directed DRAP and the health ministry to urgently revise the drug-pricing framework (Hardship Policy amendments, DRAP Policy Board composition changes); industry (citing the Supreme-Court-endorsed 2018 policy and price rises already below CPI) continues to oppose it. Still unresolved, still not enacted — a slightly more active government push than before, but no change to the GLAXO/SEARL WATCH stance. entries.basis: Monthly-timeframe accumulation zones for a 10-25yr horizon: where fundamentals + monthly support align to add in small portions. 'entry' = start nibbling at/below; 'add' = deeper monthly support to load more. Pakistan macro-aware (SBP 11.5%, KSE-100 off the Jan ATH). These are accumulation guides, not precise buy/sell signals — verify with your broker.
